data.reasoning: Both models reviewed all 3 maintainer files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, openbangla-keyboard.install). The PKGBUILD is a standard -git package that clones from the official upstream GitHub repository (OpenBangla/OpenBangla-keyboard) and performs standard build steps (cargo, cmake, make). No malicious code, network exfiltration, or injection attempts were found.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement (inconclusive vs safe) was caused entirely by a tool error in the qwen model - it received an HTTP 400 BadRequestError when attempting to audit openbangla-keyboard.install. The deepseek model successfully audited this same file and found it innocuous. This is not a genuine security disagreement but a coverage gap due to API failure.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit openbangla-keyboard.install due to LLM API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), resulting in inconclusive verdict
learnings: Tool errors (API failures) should trigger automatic retries or fallback to prevent inconclusive verdicts when other files are successfully audited
When one model has a tool error on a specific file and another model successfully audits that file, the successful audit should be weighted appropriately to resolve the disagreement

The audit system should distinguish between 'inconclusive due to tool error' and 'inconclusive due to genuine security uncertainty' - the former should not block a verdict if other models successfully covered the same files
